accepted_steps.derivation: Re-derivation of step 2 from the prose and accepted step 1. Let X_1,...,X_12 be the input bits. The givens state that they are independent and that for each i, P(X_i=1)=3/5 and P(X_i=0)=2/5. Independence means that for any fixed assignment x_1,...,x_12 in {0,1}^12, P(X_1=x_1,...,X_12=x_12)=product_{i=1}^{12} P(X_i=x_i). If the fixed string has exactly seven 1s and five 0s, then exactly seven factors are 3/5 and exactly five factors are 2/5. Finite multiplication is commutative and associative, so the product is (3/5)^7(2/5)^5, independent of which positions contain the 1s. The deterministic transitions F_0 and F_1 from step 1 act only after each bit is read and do not change the probability law or independence of the input string; they only determine the final state for each string. Thus every fixed length-12 string with exactly seven 1s has the same probability.

accepted_steps.derivation: From accepted step 1, the state space is Z4 x Z3, with 12 states, and both input symbols give deterministic transitions F0(s,t)=((s+t) mod 4,(t+1) mod 3) and F1(s,t)=((2s+t+1) mod 4,(s+t) mod 3). Define N_{k,j}(s,t) as the number of length-k input prefixes that contain exactly j ones and drive the initial state (1,0) to state (s,t). The empty prefix is length 0, has zero ones, and leaves the machine at (1,0), so N_{0,0}(1,0)=1, and all other N_{0,j}(s,t)=0. For the recurrence, take a length-(k+1) prefix with j ones ending at (s,t). Its last bit is either 0 or 1, a disjoint partition. If the last bit is 0, deleting it gives a length-k prefix with j ones ending at some (u,v) such that F0(u,v)=(s,t). Conversely, each such length-k prefix appends 0 to give a length-(k+1) prefix with j ones ending at (s,t), and distinct prefixes give distinct extensions. Thus the last-bit-0 contribution is the sum of N_{k,j}(u,v) over all (u,v) with F0(u,v)=(s,t). If the last bit is 1, deleting it gives a length-k prefix with j-1 ones ending at some (u,v) such that F1(u,v)=(s,t), and conversely appending 1 gives the required prefix. Thus the last-bit-1 contribution is the sum of N_{k,j-1}(u,v) over all (u,v) with F1(u,v)=(s,t). Adding the disjoint cases gives the recurrence, with out-of-range terms such as j-1<0 or j>k treated as zero. No probabilities are needed for this counting step.
accepted_steps.goal: Define count table N_{k,j}(s,t) as the number of length-k prefixes with j ones ending at state (s,t); initialize N_{0,0}(1,0)=1 and update by summing F_0 and F_1 transitions.
accepted_steps.result: N_{0,0}(1,0)=1 and all other N_{0,j}(s,t)=0. For k+1>=1, N_{k+1,j}(s,t)=sum over (u,v) with F0(u,v)=(s,t) of N_{k,j}(u,v) + sum over (u,v) with F1(u,v)=(s,t) of N_{k,j-1}(u,v), over Z4 x Z3, with j ranging 0..k+1 and out-of-range terms zero.
